title: Esther Chapter 7 Quiz - Multi-Level
description: An enhanced quiz on Esther chapter 7 with Easy, Medium, Hard, and Theological levels. Each level has 15 carefully crafted questions. Choose your difficulty and dive in!

easy.title: Esther Chapter 7 Quiz - Easy Level
easy.description: Perfect for beginners! Test your basic knowledge of Esther Chapter 7.

questions.question: In Esther 7, which of the following appears FIRST in the chapter?
options: The king and Haman come to banquet with Esther the queen
Esther requests her life and her people's lives
The king offers to grant Esther up to half the kingdom
Esther explains that they are sold to be destroyed
questions.correctAnswer: The king and Haman come to banquet with Esther the queen
questions.explanation: The first event mentioned in Esther 7 is in verse 1: 'So the king and Haman came to banquet with Esther the queen.'

questions.question: Who came to banquet with Esther the queen according to Esther 7:1?
questions.explanation: Esther 7:1 states, 'So the king and Haman came to banquet with Esther the queen.'

questions.question: On which day did the king speak to Esther again at the banquet of wine?
questions.explanation: Esther 7:2 says, 'And the king said again unto Esther on the second day at the banquet of wine...'

questions.question: What did the king promise Esther if she made a petition?
questions.explanation: Esther 7:2 states, 'What is thy petition, queen Esther? and it shall be granted thee...'

questions.question: What did the king say about Esther's request in Esther 7:2?
options: It shall be performed, even to the half of the kingdom
It shall be sent to the council
questions.correctAnswer: It shall be performed, even to the half of the kingdom
questions.explanation: Esther 7:2 says, 'and what is thy request? and it shall be performed, even to the half of the kingdom.'

questions.question: What did Esther ask for in her petition according to Esther 7:3?
options: Let my life be given me and my people at my request
questions.correctAnswer: Let my life be given me and my people at my request
questions.explanation: Esther 7:3 says, 'let my life be given me at my petition, and my people at my request.'

questions.question: How did Esther begin her answer to the king in Esther 7:3?
options: If I have found favour in thy sight, O king
questions.correctAnswer: If I have found favour in thy sight, O king
questions.explanation: Esther 7:3 begins, 'Then Esther the queen answered and said, If I have found favour in thy sight, O king...'

questions.question: What reason did Esther give for asking the king to save her and her people in Esther 7:4?
options: For we are sold to be destroyed, to be slain, and to perish
Because we have no other refuge
questions.correctAnswer: For we are sold to be destroyed, to be slain, and to perish
questions.explanation: Esther 7:4 states, 'For we are sold, I and my people, to be destroyed, to be slain, and to perish.'

questions.question: According to Esther 7:4, what would Esther have done if they had been sold for bondmen and bondwomen?
questions.explanation: Esther 7:4 says, 'But if we had been sold for bondmen and bondwomen, I had held my tongue...'

questions.question: What could not countervail the king's damage according to Esther 7:4?
questions.explanation: Esther 7:4 states, 'although the enemy could not countervail the king's damage.'

questions.question: Who spoke to Esther at the banquet on the second day?
questions.explanation: Esther 7:2 says, 'And the king said again unto Esther on the second day at the banquet of wine...'

questions.question: True or False: Esther asked for her own life and the lives of her people at the banquet.
questions.explanation: Esther 7:3 states, 'let my life be given me at my petition, and my people at my request,' showing she asked for both.

questions.question: True or False: The king promised Esther that her request would be performed even to half of the kingdom.
questions.explanation: Esther 7:2 says, 'and what is thy request? and it shall be performed, even to the half of the kingdom.'

questions.question: True or False: Esther said they had been sold as captives to be taken to another land.
questions.explanation: Esther 7:4 states they were sold to be destroyed, slain, and perish, not as captives to be taken elsewhere.

questions.question: True or False: Esther said she would have kept silent if they had been sold for bondmen and bondwomen.
questions.explanation: This is actually true according to Esther 7:4, so the statement is false only if negated; since the question states the statement as is, it is True, so for a False correct answer the statement must be false. Therefore this question is false as stated.

medium.title: Esther Chapter 7 Quiz - Medium Level
medium.description: Ready for more? Apply biblical truths from Esther Chapter 7 to real-life situations.

questions.question: Who did King Ahasuerus ask about during the banquet?
questions.explanation: The king asked Esther, 'Who is he, and where is he, that durst presume in his heart to do so?' referring to Haman as the one responsible for the plot against the Jews. (Esther 7:5)

questions.question: What does Esther 7:3 promise will happen if someone does what verse 7:2 commands?
options: They will receive half the kingdom
questions.correctAnswer: They will receive half the kingdom
questions.explanation: In Esther 7:2, the king promises Esther that whatever her request is, it shall be performed, even to the half of the kingdom.

questions.question: What was Haman's reaction when Esther identified him as the enemy?
questions.explanation: Esther identifies Haman as the adversary, and the verse states that 'Then Haman was afraid before the king and the queen.' (Esther 7:6)

questions.question: What does Esther 7:4 promise will happen if someone is sold for bondmen and bondwomen?
questions.explanation: Esther states that if they were sold for bondmen and bondwomen, she would have remained silent, indicating the severity of the situation regarding her people. (Esther 7:4)

questions.question: What action did the king take when he returned from the palace garden?
questions.explanation: Upon returning, the king found Haman in a compromising position with Esther and exclaimed, 'Will he force the queen also before me?' indicating his anger towards Haman. (Esther 7:8)

questions.question: How does Esther's request reflect faith in God's plan?
options: By seeking her life and her people's safety
questions.correctAnswer: By seeking her life and her people's safety
questions.explanation: Esther's petition demonstrates her faith and courage to stand up for her people, believing that God would intervene for their deliverance. (Esther 7:3)

questions.question: What does the king's wrath symbolize in the narrative?
questions.explanation: The king's wrath upon discovering Haman's plot symbolizes his role as a protector of justice for Esther and her people. (Esther 7:7)

questions.question: How can we apply Esther's bravery in our own lives?
options: By trusting God to guide us in difficult situations
By staying silent in tough times
questions.correctAnswer: By trusting God to guide us in difficult situations
questions.explanation: Esther's courage to speak out for her people encourages us to have faith and trust in God when facing our challenges. (Esther 7:3)

questions.question: What lesson can be learned from Haman's downfall?
questions.explanation: Haman's pride and evil plans ultimately led to his downfall when the king turned against him. (Esther 7:6-8)

questions.question: What does Esther's plea reveal about her priorities?
options: Her safety and her people's survival
Her wish for a lavish banquet
questions.correctAnswer: Her safety and her people's survival
questions.explanation: Esther's heartfelt plea to save her life and the lives of her people shows her deep concern for their welfare over personal gain. (Esther 7:3)

questions.question: What was the king's reaction to Haman's actions towards Esther?
questions.explanation: The king's anger towards Haman for his actions against Esther indicates a strong protective instinct and sense of justice. (Esther 7:8)

questions.question: What does Esther's story teach about the importance of advocacy?
options: It can lead to life-saving outcomes
questions.correctAnswer: It can lead to life-saving outcomes
questions.explanation: Esther's advocacy for her people not only saved her own life but also the lives of many, illustrating the power of standing up for what is right. (Esther 7:3)

questions.question: True or False: Haman was confident in his actions before Esther exposed him.
questions.explanation: Haman's confidence was evident until Esther revealed him as the enemy, causing him to fear for his life. (Esther 7:6)

questions.question: True or False: The king always trusted Haman without question.
questions.explanation: The king's reaction to Haman's actions indicates that he did not blindly trust him and was capable of anger and judgment against him. (Esther 7:8)

questions.question: True or False: Esther was afraid to confront the king about her people.
questions.explanation: Despite the risk, Esther displayed courage in confronting the king about the threat to her people. (Esther 7:3)

hard.title: Esther Chapter 7 Quiz - Hard Level
hard.description: Challenge yourself with deep analysis and cross-biblical connections from Esther Chapter 7.

questions.question: What did Harbonah reveal to the king regarding Haman's actions?
options: Haman had prepared a feast for the king.
Haman had made gallows for Mordecai.
Haman had stolen from the king.
Haman was planning to attack the queen.
questions.correctAnswer: Haman had made gallows for Mordecai.
questions.explanation: This answer is correct because Esther 7:9 states that Harbonah pointed out the gallows Haman had made for Mordecai, which was a pivotal moment leading to Haman's execution.

questions.question: What was the king's command regarding Haman after he learned the truth from Esther?
questions.explanation: The king commanded that Haman be hanged on the gallows he had prepared for Mordecai, as stated in Esther 7:9.

questions.question: How did the king react after discovering Haman's intentions?
questions.explanation: The king's wrath was evident when he arose in anger after hearing Esther's revelation about Haman, as indicated in Esther 7:7.

questions.question: What was Haman's demeanor before the king as he realized his fate?
questions.explanation: Haman was afraid before the king and queen after Esther exposed him, as noted in Esther 7:6.

questions.question: What did the king do after he left the banquet in wrath?
options: He sought counsel from his advisors.
He went into the palace garden.
He called for a new banquet.
questions.correctAnswer: He went into the palace garden.
questions.explanation: Esther 7:7 states that the king arose from the banquet of wine and went into the palace garden in his wrath.

questions.question: What was the outcome of Haman's execution?
questions.explanation: According to Esther 7:10, after Haman was hanged, the king's anger was calmed.

questions.question: What does the Hebrew word 'gallows' in Esther 7:9 mean?
questions.explanation: The Hebrew word for 'gallows' refers specifically to a structure used for hanging, as indicated in Esther 7:9.

questions.question: Which literary technique is used in Esther 7:7 when the king arises in wrath?
questions.explanation: The king's rising in wrath foreshadows the impending judgment on Haman, establishing dramatic tension in the narrative.

questions.question: Which other Bible passage connects to Esther 7:4 regarding the persecution of God's people?
questions.explanation: Exodus 1:22 reflects the historical context of God's people facing extermination, paralleling Esther's plea for her people in Esther 7:4.

questions.question: Which other Bible passage connects to Esther 7:6 regarding the exposure of evil?
questions.explanation: Luke 8:17 emphasizes that nothing hidden will remain secret, similar to Esther's revelation of Haman's wickedness in Esther 7:6.

questions.question: What precedes Esther 7:9 regarding Haman's actions?
options: The king asking Haman for his opinion.
Esther identifying Haman as the enemy.
Haman preparing a feast for the king.
questions.correctAnswer: Esther identifying Haman as the enemy.
questions.explanation: Esther 7:6 shows Esther revealing Haman as the adversary before the king's subsequent command in Esther 7:9.

questions.question: What follows Esther 7:10 regarding the resolution of the king's wrath?
options: The decree against the Jews was lifted.
questions.correctAnswer: The decree against the Jews was lifted.
questions.explanation: The resolution of Haman's fate led to a subsequent decree concerning the safety of the Jews, which follows logically after Esther 7:10.

questions.question: The statement 'So they hanged Haman on the gallows' is an example of what literary device?
questions.explanation: It is ironic that Haman, who plotted to hang Mordecai, meets the same fate he intended for another, highlighting the theme of poetic justice.

questions.question: Haman was hanged for his plot against Mordecai. True or False?
questions.explanation: Haman was indeed hanged for plotting against Mordecai, as stated in Esther 7:10.

questions.question: The king showed mercy to Haman by not executing him. True or False?
questions.explanation: The king did not show mercy; instead, he ordered Haman's execution, confirming his wrath as noted in Esther 7:9-10.

theological.title: Esther Chapter 7 Quiz - Theological Level
theological.description: Deep biblical theology from Esther Chapter 7 that unites all believers. Explore foundational truths about God, creation, and humanity.

questions.question: What doctrine does Esther 7:3 teach about salvation in the context of corporate identity and intercession?
options: Salvation involves individualistic faith without concern for others
Intercession for one’s people is vital as their fate is intertwined with the believer's
Salvation is only about personal deliverance, not national or communal
Only rulers can intercede for the salvation of their people
questions.correctAnswer: Intercession for one’s people is vital as their fate is intertwined with the believer's
questions.explanation: Esther 7:3 shows Esther pleading not only for her own life but for her people, indicating the doctrine that salvation has a corporate dimension where intercession plays a critical role.

questions.question: What doctrine about divine justice is illustrated in Esther 7:10?
options: God’s justice is delayed indefinitely until the end of time
God’s justice can be mediated through human authorities and immediate
God ignores human wrongdoing and allows evil to prosper
Divine justice is only symbolic and not enacted in history
questions.correctAnswer: God’s justice can be mediated through human authorities and immediate
questions.explanation: Esther 7:10 demonstrates that the king’s wrath is pacified by the execution of Haman on his own gallows, illustrating that divine justice can manifest through earthly rulers swiftly.

questions.question: What doctrine regarding human sin and pride is taught in Esther 7:6?
options: Sinful pride leads to fear and downfall before divine authority
Human sin is irrelevant to the unfolding of divine plans
Pride secures one’s favor before the king
Sin is only punished in the afterlife, not in this life
questions.correctAnswer: Sinful pride leads to fear and downfall before divine authority
questions.explanation: In Esther 7:6, Haman’s fear before the king and queen after being exposed as wicked illustrates the doctrine that prideful sin leads to exposure and downfall before divine and kingly authority.

questions.question: Which divine attribute does Esther 7:5 specifically demonstrate?
questions.explanation: Esther 7:5 shows the king questioning who dared to oppose him, reflecting God’s attribute of sovereignty as the ultimate authority over human affairs.

questions.question: Which divine attribute is most evident in Esther 7:7 when the king moves to the garden in wrath?
questions.explanation: Esther 7:7 depicts the king’s wrath rising to action, illustrating the divine attribute of righteous wrath against evil.

questions.question: How does Esther 7:9 connect to the broader biblical theme of divine retribution and protection of the righteous?
options: It shows that human schemes are more powerful than God’s protection
It fulfills the theme that God protects those who speak for the king and punishes their enemies
It denies any connection between human justice and divine justice
It teaches that the righteous must always be silent to avoid danger
questions.correctAnswer: It fulfills the theme that God protects those who speak for the king and punishes their enemies
questions.explanation: Harbonah’s mention of the gallows prepared for Mordecai in Esther 7:9 connects to the theme of divine protection for the righteous and punishment of the wicked, consistent with Scripture's justice motifs.

questions.question: How does the narrative of Esther 7:4–6 prepare for the New Testament teaching on intercessory prayer and spiritual warfare?
options: It discourages intercession for others, focusing only on oneself
It models the necessity of standing boldly before rulers for the sake of one’s people
It teaches that spiritual warfare is irrelevant to earthly matters
It emphasizes that prayer has no effect on political decisions
questions.correctAnswer: It models the necessity of standing boldly before rulers for the sake of one’s people
questions.explanation: Esther 7:4–6 shows Esther boldly identifying Haman as the enemy and pleading for her people, prefiguring New Testament teachings on intercessory prayer and spiritual confrontation.

questions.question: What combined doctrine do verses Esther 7:8 and Esther 7:9 teach about the justice of God against human evil?
options: God’s justice is arbitrary and unrelated to human actions
God’s justice uses human instruments to reverse evil plots and vindicate the innocent
God ignores human evil when it is politically expedient
God’s justice is only eschatological and not historic
questions.correctAnswer: God’s justice uses human instruments to reverse evil plots and vindicate the innocent
questions.explanation: Esther 7:8–9 shows the king’s intervention stopping Haman’s abuse and ordering his execution on the gallows made for Mordecai, teaching that God’s justice employs human agents to punish evil.

questions.question: What combined doctrine about human sin and divine wrath is taught in Esther 7:7 and Esther 7:10?
options: Human sin goes unpunished and divine wrath is ineffective
Divine wrath is just and results in the punishment of evil-doers in history
Human sin is always overlooked by God in favor of mercy
Divine wrath is only symbolic and not enacted through history
questions.correctAnswer: Divine wrath is just and results in the punishment of evil-doers in history
questions.explanation: Esther 7:7 shows the king’s wrath rising against Haman, and Esther 7:10 shows Haman’s execution, teaching that divine wrath is just and enacted historically against human sin.

questions.question: What combined theological insight do Esther 7:2 and Esther 7:3 provide about God’s providence and human agency in salvation history?
options: God’s providence excludes human agency completely
Human agency is irrelevant because God’s will is arbitrary
God providentially places human agents who must courageously act for salvation to be realized
Salvation depends only on political power without divine involvement
questions.correctAnswer: God providentially places human agents who must courageously act for salvation to be realized
questions.explanation: Esther 7:2 and 7:3 show the king’s offer to grant requests and Esther’s bold petition for her people, revealing God’s providence in placing human agents who must exercise faithful courage.

questions.question: Sceptics claim the execution of Haman in Esther 7:9-10 shows a vindictive and unjust God. What does this passage actually teach?
options: It reflects divine justice executed through human authority against a confirmed enemy of God’s people
It endorses revenge as a human right without divine sanction
It shows God arbitrarily punishing without cause
It illustrates that God is indifferent to human evil
questions.correctAnswer: It reflects divine justice executed through human authority against a confirmed enemy of God’s people
questions.explanation: Esther 7:9-10 shows Haman executed on the gallows he prepared for Mordecai, demonstrating just retribution against evil, consistent with God’s justice rather than vindictiveness.

questions.question: What doctrine concerning the nature of God’s covenant faithfulness is illustrated in Esther 7:1?
options: God is unfaithful and forgetful of His promises
God’s faithfulness is revealed through sovereign acts involving His covenant people
God’s covenant is irrelevant to political events
God’s promises are conditional on human merit alone
questions.correctAnswer: God’s faithfulness is revealed through sovereign acts involving His covenant people
questions.explanation: The banquet in Esther 7:1 sets the stage for God’s faithful intervention on behalf of His people, illustrating His covenant faithfulness in history.

questions.question: Which divine attribute does Esther 7:4 best exemplify in the face of impending destruction?
questions.explanation: Esther 7:4’s plea for life amidst a decree of destruction highlights God’s attribute of mercy toward His people.

questions.question: How does Esther 7:8 contribute to the theological theme of divine protection of the queen as a type of Christ’s protection of His bride?
options: It shows the queen abandoned and defenseless
It demonstrates divine protection acting through earthly authority to defend the queen’s dignity
It denies any special protection for the queen
It teaches that the queen must rely only on her own strength
questions.correctAnswer: It demonstrates divine protection acting through earthly authority to defend the queen’s dignity
questions.explanation: In Esther 7:8 the king’s reaction to Haman’s attempt against Esther reveals God’s providential protection of the queen, prefiguring Christ’s protection of His bride.

questions.question: What combined theological truth do Esther 7:5 and Esther 7:7 reveal about God’s control over human wrath and the purposes of judgment?
options: God loses control over human emotions and judgments
God sovereignly directs human wrath to serve His righteous judgment
Human wrath is always sinful and should be suppressed
Judgment is random and disconnected from God’s purposes
questions.correctAnswer: God sovereignly directs human wrath to serve His righteous judgment
questions.explanation: Esther 7:5 and 7:7 show the king’s wrath rising against Haman after Esther’s petition, demonstrating God’s sovereignty in directing human emotions to accomplish just ends.
